newsitem.title: USA: Chip equipment group says Nov. book-to-bill rises.
newsitem.headline: Chip equipment group says Nov. book-to-bill rises.

text.p: Semiconductor Equipment and Materials International, an industry group, said its November book-to-bill ratio for North American equipment makers, rose to 0.87 from 0.77 in October.
The ratio compares product orders to shipments during the month. A book-to-bill figure of 0.87 means $87 in orders were received for each $100 worth of products shipped.

Orders for semiconductor making machinery jumped to $936.5 million in November, a 14 percent rise from October levels. Shipments totaled $1.08 billion, about even with revised October results but 12 percent below year ago levels.

"The improvement in order levels could be an indication that the semiconductor equipment industry has hit the bottom of the current down cycle," Elizabeth Schumann, senior market analyst for the group, said in a statement issued late on Tuesday.
The group's book-to-bill is a ratio of three-month moving average bookings to three-month moving average shipments.
